Selected work

Built around the problem, not the stack.

Each of these solves a specific business problem: following up with every lead, answering questions from your own documents, turning a website visit into an inquiry. Pick the one closest to yours and I'll build something like it.

When a new lead comes in, an AI agent writes a personal follow-up, emails it, and logs the lead in a Google Sheet. Nobody has to chase. It runs on n8n, with Groq writing the reply and Gmail and Google Sheets handling sending and tracking.

n8n · Groq · Gemini · Gmail · Google Sheets

Visit the site ↗

A 24/7 AI sales system built for roofing contractors. It picks up every call and form, qualifies the homeowner, books the inspection straight to the calendar, and logs the lead — built to keep up when storm season sends 100 leads in 48 hours.

Vapi · Make.com · Cal.com · Google Sheets · Gmail

Visit the site ↗

Guests browse retreats, send inquiries and chat with an AI assistant. Every inquiry lands in a lead-management view, so the owner can follow up and nothing gets missed.

Next.js · TypeScript · Prisma · Groq

Live demo ↗

Upload PDFs, docs or notes. Groundwork searches by keyword and by meaning, re-ranks the results, then writes an answer that cites where it came from. When free hosting kept wiping the search index, I moved storage to Qdrant Cloud so it stays online.

Ragas — 1.00 faithfulness · 0.71 answer relevancy

Instead of one oversized model response, the review runs as coordinated steps: triage, review, and escalation of risky changes (like auth or payments) to a human. It comes with a React dashboard, sign-in and live monitoring.

Questions before we start

Here’s what I get asked.

I build. I work across the interface, backend, APIs, databases, integrations, testing, and AI layer rather than stopping at the design file.

Design-aware · Full-stack

Yes. I can start from a rough idea, an existing design, a specification, a repository, or a partial product and take the work through implementation, testing, and delivery.

Idea → Working software

We start by understanding the problem and desired outcome, then move through scope, design, engineering, testing, deployment, and iteration. The pace changes with the project; the discipline stays the same.

Clear scope · Direct communication

It depends on the surface area and constraints. I prefer breaking the work into clear milestones, validating the risky parts early, then shipping in useful increments instead of waiting for one large final handoff.

Milestones · Incremental delivery

That is enough to start. We can use the first conversation to clarify the audience, problem, desired outcome, constraints, and the smallest useful version worth building.

Discovery · Product framing

Yes. I can work inside an existing repository, design system, API surface, or delivery process and contribute without forcing the team into a completely new stack.

Existing teams · Existing codebases

For selected builds, yes. That can include fixes, measurement, small improvements, and the next iteration after real users start interacting with the product.

Support · Measure · Improve

I’m open to full-time software engineering roles and selected product builds where I can take meaningful ownership. Remote-first works best, with Pune also possible for a strong fit.

Remote-first · Full-time + selected builds
